title: Ranson's Criteria (Acute Pancreatitis)
sources: Ranson JH et al. Surg Gynecol Obstet 1974; ACG 2013 acute pancreatitis guideline

changelog.change: Initial entry — from ED_ICU_OR_Calculators.xlsx. Non-gallstone (original) criteria.

purpose: Predicts mortality in acute pancreatitis. Five criteria are assessed at admission and six more at 48 hours — the score is only complete at 48 h, which is its main practical limitation. BISAP or the APACHE II / persistent SIRS are more useful early. Use Ranson as a 48-h severity checkpoint.

items.label: 48 HOURS — BUN rise > 5 mg/dL (1.8 mmol/L) despite fluids

interpretation.label: Mortality ~ 0–3%. Predicted mild course — ward care, aggressive early goal-directed crystalloid, early enteral feeding as tolerated, analgesia, treat the cause
Mortality ~ 15%. Predicted severe pancreatitis — HDU/ICU-level monitoring, meticulous fluid resuscitation with frequent reassessment, watch for organ failure and local complications
Mortality ~ 40%. Severe — ICU, organ support, early involvement of a pancreatitis / surgical team; CT with contrast at 72–96 h if not improving
Mortality ~ 100% in the original series. Critical illness — full organ support, goals-of-care discussion

notes: Gallstone-pancreatitis cutoffs differ (age > 70, WBC > 18, glucose > 220, AST > 250, LDH > 400; 48-h: Hct fall > 10, BUN rise > 2, Ca < 8, base deficit > 5, fluid sequestration > 4 L; no PaO2). Persistent organ failure beyond 48 h (Revised Atlanta 'moderately severe / severe') is the modern determinant of outcome — do not wait for a Ranson score to escalate a deteriorating patient.
buildNote: Additive, 11 criteria × 1 point (5 admission + 6 at 48 h). Original non-gallstone thresholds.
